mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns vanishes (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the joint significance of GDPC1 and HOUST is not statistically robust (p > 0.15 in bivariate regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which elevates wage and input costs, eroding profit margins and ultimately producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as investors anticipate margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained low unemployment, or the relationship reverses (positive correlation).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals weakening manufacturing output and lower corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO contraction episodes (p > 0.10), or the effect reverses in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% signals a deflationary monetary regime, which historically has been associated with equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (p > 0.10), or the joint effect is not statistically distinguishable from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 0.5% over four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during such episodes (p > 0.10), or the effect reverses in more than 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 0.2% in the same month signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change > 0.1% AND PAYEMS monthly change < -0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (p > 0.10), or the joint signal fails to outperform a single-proxy threshold in predictive power.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.7% for three consecutive months signals a recovery in manufacturing activity and higher corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.7% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during such episodes (p > 0.10), or the effect reverses in more than 50% of triggered periods.
